headline: Shakib Al Hasan ready to return and face trial if security is guaranteed
summary: The former Bangladesh captain says he is willing to return from exile to face murder and corruption charges, provided the government ensures his safety.
details: Former Bangladesh captain Shakib Al Hasan has expressed his readiness to return home from a two-year exile to face trial on charges including murder, provided the government guarantees his security.
Shakib, a former lawmaker for the Awami League, has been living in the United States since the government of Sheikh Hasina was toppled in August 2024 following a student-led uprising.

He told Reuters that he is keen to return and face the court trials, stating, "I know I haven't done anything," and expressed a desire to play a farewell series and represent Bangladesh in the 2027 World Cup.
The cricketer currently faces two active cases: one regarding the alleged killing of a protester during the uprising and another involving alleged corruption.
Shakib described the murder case as "laughable," noting that it was filed on a day in August 2024 when he was playing a match in Toronto.

He revealed that a previous attempt to return in late 2024 failed after he was told mid-journey to turn back, and a later plan collapsed after he posted a birthday message for Sheikh Hasina on social media.
Shakib has rejected suggestions that distancing himself from the Awami League would ease his return, stating there is no way he would consider that.
He is currently playing franchise cricket in Sri Lanka and has expressed a desire to discuss his return with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
caption:
Shakib Al Hasan is ready to return to Bangladesh and face trial for murder and corruption charges—but only if his safety is guaranteed.

Former Bangladesh captain Shakib Al Hasan has expressed his readiness to return home from a two-year exile to face trial on charges including murder, provided the government guarantees his security.

Shakib, a former lawmaker for the Awami League, has been living in the United States since the government of Sheikh Hasina was toppled in August 2024 following a student-led uprising.

He told Reuters that he is keen to return and face the court trials, stating, "I know I haven't done anything," and expressed a desire to play a farewell series and represent Bangladesh in the 2027 World Cup.

The cricketer currently faces two active cases: one regarding the alleged killing of a protester during the uprising and another involving alleged corruption.

Shakib described the murder case as "laughable," noting that it was filed on a day in August 2024 when he was playing a match in Toronto.

He revealed that a previous attempt to return in late 2024 failed after he was told mid-journey to turn back, and a later plan collapsed after he posted a birthday message for Sheikh Hasina on social media.

Shakib has rejected suggestions that distancing himself from the Awami League would ease his return, stating there is no way he would consider that.

He is currently playing franchise cricket in Sri Lanka and has expressed a desire to discuss his return with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

headline: Sheikh Hasina announces plan to return to Bangladesh in December
summary: The ousted prime minister shared her intention to return during a virtual press conference in New Delhi, sparking reactions from analysts and the Bangladesh government.
details: Sheikh Hasina, the former prime minister ousted during the student-led uprising, announced her intention to return to Bangladesh this December. She made the announcement during a virtual press conference organized by the Foreign Correspondents' Club (FCC) South Asia in New Delhi.

The Bangladesh government has expressed strong reactions to the Indian government for allowing Hasina to hold the press conference. Bangladesh has repeatedly requested India to extradite the former prime minister, who is a fugitive accused of crimes against humanity.

Analysts suggest several reasons for her announcement. Some believe she wants to maintain her political relevance and reactivate the banned Awami League, while others suggest she may want to clear her name in court or simply spend her final days in her home country.

However, critics and political experts warn that her return could trigger significant instability. Professor Mohammad Jalal Uddin Sikder noted that the government is not prepared to receive her and that her presence could lead to political unrest.

Michael Kugelman of the Atlantic Council stated that Hasina would almost certainly be arrested upon arrival at the airport. He warned that her return could mobilize both supporters and opponents, increasing the risk of violent clashes.
The Bangladesh government remains firm on its stance. Prime Minister's advisor Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the government is ready to ensure justice and welcomes her return to face the legal process.
